data.title: Contact Energy chair departs after year of accelerated renewable investment and sector warnings
data.description:
An announcement from Contact Energy Limited ( (NZ:CEN) ) is now available.

Contact Energy’s outgoing chair used the annual shareholder meeting to highlight a “very strong” year marked by bold decisions, accelerated investment and continued growth, underpinned by the Contact26 decarbonisation strategy and the new Contact31+ plan to lead New Zealand’s renewable energy future. The chair emphasised that major investments in geothermal, solar, batteries and the Manawa Energy acquisition have strengthened flexibility and resilience, positioning the company to meet rising demand for clean energy.

The address placed Contact’s transformation within a broader sector context, arguing that New Zealand’s electricity industry is investing at record levels in new renewable capacity despite criticism and that wholesale prices have fallen around 30%, supporting economic resilience. The chair warned that ideologically driven policies, such as the 2018 oil and gas ban or further structural separation of gentailers, risk undermining investment and ultimately raising consumer costs.

data.title: Liberty Puerto Rico considers standalone structure amid debt talks
data.description:
An update from Liberty Global LiLAC ( (LILA) ) is now available.

Liberty Latin America disclosed that negotiations with certain secured lenders of its Puerto Rico unit over a potential restructuring of term loans, senior secured notes due 2027 and 2029, and related UnSub facilities have taken place but are no longer ongoing. On September 11, 2026, a creditor steering committee counterproposal outlined a structure that would reconsolidate existing entities, refinance $410 million of UnSub debt with new first‑out financing, and potentially separate Liberty Puerto Rico into a standalone “New LPR.”

The latest term sheets detail a mix of new money first‑out notes or term loans, extended revolving credit facility terms, and second‑out takeback debt capped around 4.0x leverage, alongside significant equity reallocation to participating first‑lien creditors. Liberty Latin America’s retained stake would be largely reduced or reshaped through minority equity and warrant rights, signalling a possible shift in control of the Puerto Rico operations and material implications for recoveries across the company’s secured creditor base, although no binding agreement has yet been reached.

data.title: ChowChow Cloud Shareholders Back Reverse Split, Dual-Class Structure and Massive Capital Increase
data.description:

On September 14, 2026, ChowChow Cloud International Holdings Ltd. shareholders approved a 10-for-1 reverse share split of authorized, issued and unissued ordinary shares, with no fractional shares to be issued and directors empowered to resolve rounding via capitalizing reserves. Investors also backed the creation of dual-class stock with single-vote Class A shares and ten-vote Class B shares, together with a redesignation of existing issued and unissued shares into the new classes.

The meeting further endorsed a massive increase in authorized share capital to US$100 billion, enabling the issuance of up to 100 trillion shares split between the new A and B classes. Shareholders approved a second amended and restated memorandum and articles of association to reflect the capital changes and a lower threshold for written ordinary resolutions, and authorized the board to complete all related corporate and regulatory filings, consolidating management’s control and strategic flexibility.

data.title: JBS S.A. and VIVA to Form Joint Leather Venture JBS VIVA
data.description:
